topics.label: Course introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, its interdisciplinary audience, and the key learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of genetic regulation and tissue differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer at the cellular and tissue levels as a breakdown of normal differentiation programs and architecture driven by accumulated mutations.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, malignancy, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between benign and malignant tumors through tissue invasion, metastatic progression, and standardized naming conventions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physiological and mechanical processes by which primary and metastatic tumors impair organ function and cause death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across tissues and species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the frequency, tissue distribution, and mortality rates of tumors in human populations and across animal taxa.

topics.label: Cancer detection and clinical screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, methods, and varying effectiveness of population screening across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and learning outcomes review
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reiterating the learning outcomes and providing logistical closing remarks for upcoming sessions.
